mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Corporate Status / Certificate of Good Standing for each corporate limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registrar in each corporate partner's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if jurisdiction is party to the Hague Apostille Convention), otherwise Consular Legalization by a Canadian embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney / Representation Certificate executed by non-resident partners appointing the Quebec agent to file the declaration of registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Qualified notary public or lawyer in the foreign partner's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable, with certified French translation for Quebec registry filing

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of each partner's constitutional documents or partnership deed (e.g., by-laws, memorandum, articles)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Service of corporate registry or notarial office in jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; translation by a member of the Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interprètes agréés du Québec (OTTIAQ)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory FINTRAC-compliant customer due diligence, identity verification, and politically exposed person (PEP) assessment (domestic and foreign PEPs) for all partners, including beneficial owners, as set out in the PCMLTFA and FINTRAC guidance; required screening of all partners, directors, and senior officers against the United Nations Act sanctions list, Special Economic Measures Act lists, the Canadian Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act list, and, as best practice for cross-border aviation finance and correspondent payments, the OFAC SDN list and EU/UK consolidated lists; for medium-risk air cargo charter brokering, enhanced scrutiny applies to any cash-intensive transactions, cargo charter payments routed through high-risk jurisdictions, and use of third-party agents.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online services at https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Quebec Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11) requires that any registered enterprise name, including a limited partnership declared in Quebec, be in French. A name in another language may be accepted only if it is accompanied by a French version, and the French version must be used for the primary legal publicity. Roman-script transliteration is not a substitute for a French-language name; however, a grammatical French version that is not a pure transliteration is accepted, subject to registration by the Registrar.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Cooperative (without authorization under the Cooperatives Act)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: After a name rejection by the Registraire des entreprises, the applicant may file a request for reconsideration with the Registrar setting out the grounds for legal validity of the proposed name. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may, within 60 days of notification, appeal administratively under section 116.1 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1) and, ultimately, proceed before the Cour du Québec within ordinary delay rules; the Registrar publishes an administrative decision and the name reservation fee is not refunded on rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted with practical limitations: Quebec law requires the declaration of registration to identify an establishment (adresse d'établissement) in Quebec where books and records may be inspected and service may be made. A virtual office address is generally accepted by the Registraire des entreprises for service-of-process and correspondence purposes, provided it is a bona fide physical address in Quebec and not merely a mail-forwarding post-office box. For air-cargo charter brokerage, banks and Transport Canada may refuse to accept a purely virtual office without physical management presence; industry practice requires a designated Quebec agent and records custodian.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (~5-10%) during the pre-revenue formation phase; moderate-to-high (~25-40% annual assessment) upon obtaining air cargo/freight forwarding operating credentials or cargo charter authority under Canadian aviation regulations, where the provincial regulator or transport ministry may conduct unannounced examinations of the registered establishment.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing per-page certified translation market rate in Quebec (approx. CAD 45-60/page)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial fee schedule and Canadian consular services tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization chain for foreign partner documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Government-issued tariff for apostille/certification plus courier and processing agency fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office provider (annual virtual office service in Quebec)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed registered office / service address provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing commercial market benchmark in Montreal/Quebec for service-of-process address and mail handling

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: External counsel legal due diligence and preparation of partnership declaration and UBO disclosure
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Quebec law firm or licensed corporate agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed fee based on partner count; standard corporate governance retainer for a two-partner LP with foreign corporate partners

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, arts. 2236-2245 (société en commandite); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-45, ss. 19-30
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Registrar of Enterprises for Québec)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Registration (Déclaration d'immatriculation) for a limited partnership
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Québec limited partnership; capital is fixed by the partnership agreement and no escrow account is required for air cargo brokerage activities.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the corporate partnership agreement of Air Cargo Charter Broker LP dated [date] is ratified, including the subscription of partnership units by each limited partner in the amounts set forth in Schedule A, and the General Partner is authorized to call all capital contributions. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the partnership is established at [address], City of Montréal, Province of Québec, and [name] is appointed as attorney for service of process. RESOLVED, that [name] is appointed Chief Executive Officer, [name] Chief Financial Officer, and [name] Corporate Secretary, all with authority to execute filings with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and banking documentation. RESOLVED, that the General Partner is empowered to open bank accounts, retain counsel, and complete CTA and IATA accreditation filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) online services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a legal name search through the REQ online portal; verify the proposed name includes 'Société en commandite' or 'S.E.C.' (or 'Limited Partnership'/'L.P.'), is not confusingly similar, and complies with the naming provisions of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. Reserve the name online if the partnership intends a name that differs from the disclosure of partners.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend the proposed name by adding a distinct element, re-submit the reservation request, or file an objection if a conflicting third-party right is asserted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Parties (General Partner and Limited Partners) under the Civil Code of Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute a written partnership agreement containing the legal name, Québec registered office, description of business (air freight forwarding and cargo charter brokerage), capital contributions, profit and loss allocation, management powers of the General Partner, restriction on limited partners participating in control, indemnification, and dissolution terms. The agreement need not be notarized unless involving real property transfers or similar formalities.
required_dossiers: Identified partners' passports or national IDs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend the partnership agreement by unanimous written consent of partners; re-execute pages containing corrected terms.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the REQ online filing portal and complete the 'Declaration of Registration' (Déclaration d'immatriculation) for a 'société en commandite'. Enter the partnership name, establishment address in Québec, legal form, description of activities, and information on the General Partner and each Limited Partner as required by CQLR c. P-45. Pay the prescribed fee, then download the 'Attestation de l'immatriculation' containing the eight-digit NEQ (Numéro d'entreprise du Québec).
required_dossiers: Partnership agreement excerpt identifying the General Partner
Proof of registered office in Québec (lease, utility bill, or letter of consent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to REQ notice of deficiency within ten calendar days; file a corrective declaration through the REQ portal without requiring a new entity number, and provide any missing partner identification or lease documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for Canadian and Québec tax accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency and Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Attestation de l'immatriculation, apply to the Canada Revenue Agency for a Business Number (BN) and GST/HST account, and, where applicable, import/export account; file a separate Revenu Québec QST registration. Appoint the General Partner as the responsible taxpayer, disclose the partnership's pass-through status, and provide bank or principal contacts.
required_dossiers: Fiscal identification of the General Partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Provide corrective information through the CRA/Revenu Québec business registration portal; verify that the General Partner's SIN/BN matches REQ records; file a QST/GST registration amendment where applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening commercial banking and completing regulatory notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner and authorized financial institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a Canadian commercial bank account in the partnership's name with the General Partner as signing officer, pass KYC documentation, and provide anti-money laundering declarations consistent with the medium-risk rating for freight forwarding. Notify the Canadian Transportation Agency in writing of the formation as a non-carrier charter brokerage and confirm that no air carrier operating license is held.
required_dossiers: General Partner's corporate resolutions or equivalent authorization
Bank KYC forms and proof of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve beneficial ownership gaps identified by bank compliance, amend the account mandate by a partner resolution, or transition to another Canadian-licensed bank accepting the existing REQ file.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Canadian Transportation Agency (CTA) – Licensing and Compliance Division
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Air Cargo Charter Broker Registration (Non-Carrier Freight Forwarding)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – administrative office activity; no full EIA or environmental registration required under section 22 of the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c. Q-2)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office operations produce no regulated wastewater or VOC point-source discharges; the premises must comply with municipal wastewater discharge by-laws and municipal recyclable/organic waste sorting standards. If the partner arrangement ever includes an aircraft, engine idling, or a cargo terminal, separate Clean Air Act and fuel storage permits would be triggered.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and occupancy certificate from the local fire prevention bureau; workplace health and safety registration with the CNESST (Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail); structural load and architectural access compliance for the leased office with no special loading requirement, and, if applicable, inspection of any hoisting or lifting apparatus used for warehouse ancillary services.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), constituted under the Bank of Canada Act; prudential bank supervision by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); anti-money-laundering and cross-border transfer monitoring by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC). No standalone foreign exchange administration exists because Canada maintains complete current and capital account convertibility with no exchange control approvals.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current and capital account convertibility under Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement. The Canadian dollar (CAD) is a free-floating currency, and no exchange control filings are required for inbound foreign direct investment, non-resident limited partner capital contributions, or outbound profit and partnership distributions. Remittance frictions are limited to tax compliance: Part XIII withholding tax on certain Canadian-source payments to non-resident partners (e.g., interest, royalties, management fees) and Part XIV branch tax on unremitted Canadian business income, subject to treaty relief under the Canada–US Tax Convention and other bilateral treaties. Quebec imposes no provincial exchange controls but requires the limited partnership to maintain active registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and to satisfy Revenu Québec tax registration and reporting requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Canada imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no obligation to repatriate export receipts. An air cargo charter broker may freely retain proceeds in foreign currency. Mandatory reporting obligations that apply are limited to: (i) FINTRAC cross-border electronic funds transfer reports for each incoming or outgoing wire transfer of C$10,000 or more; (ii) International Transactions Reporting System (ITRS) data collection by financial institutions for balance-of-payments statistics; and (iii) Canada Revenue Agency foreign-asset and foreign-income reporting, including Form T1135 where foreign account balances exceed prescribed thresholds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
Laurentian Bank of Canada (Banque Laurentienne du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium as a primary treasury banking rail and Medium-to-High as a supplementary payments channel. An offshore digital electronic money institution (EMI) may not take deposits or carry on banking business in Canada unless licensed as a Schedule I or Schedule II bank under the Bank Act. Offshore EMIs may operate only as money services businesses (MSBs) registered with FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) and, in Quebec, may require additional registration or licensing from the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) for money-services and currency-exchange activities. An offshore EMI can provide payment initiation, digital wallet settlement, and commercial card services through a licensed Canadian Schedule I bank partner, but it cannot offer insured CAD deposit accounts or direct access to Lynx RTGS. For the ISIC 5229 air cargo charter broker model, the viable fintech structure is a combined treasury architecture: a Canadian Schedule I bank as the settlement and escrow backbone, with a FINTRAC-registered EMI used for merchant payments, fuel-card settlement, and small-value cross-border disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a foreign limited partnership with non-resident partners and foreign-based directors, dominant Canadian bank practice requires at least one physical appearance by the general partner, an authorized signatory, or an attorney-in-fact before a Canadian branch representative or a Canadian notary to satisfy FINTRAC client-identification duties under the PCMLTFA. Remote account opening is selectively permitted where: (i) the signatory holds a valid Canadian-issued photo identity document or a passport of equivalent reliability; (ii) electronic identity verification is completed through a recognized Canadian KYC utility; (iii) the partnership agreement and corporate resolutions are notarized and legalized; and (iv) the LP maintains a registered Canadian office address with evidence of substance. Pure remote onboarding is generally rejected for non-resident entities lacking Canadian economic presence. Quebec-based banks, notably National Bank of Canada and Laurentian Bank, may require an in-person verification session at a Montreal or Quebec City branch before the initial account activation. The prudent and reproducible path is a physical closing meeting in Montreal conducted by the general partner or a designated attorney-in-fact holding a notarized general power of attorney, accompanied by original corporate and partnership documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident partners concentrated in tax-haven or high-risk jurisdictions in the beneficial-ownership cascade
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified true copies of passports; tax residency certificates issued by the relevant tax authorities; a complete beneficial-ownership chain table depicting each general and limited partner through to the ultimate natural persons; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements; the signed limited partnership agreement; and written legal opinions from the foreign counsel of each non-resident partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payments or channeled funds that appear inconsistent with the air-cargo charter brokerage revenue model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed aircraft charter agreements, brokerage service contracts, proforma invoices, air waybills and bills of lading, operator invoices, fuel-supplier invoices, and ground-handling invoices; a transaction-velocity narrative explaining expected payment flows; and a rolling 12-month business plan with volumes and counterparty names.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of a virtual office, registered-agent address, or bare post office box as the partnership's principal place of business
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: An executed commercial lease in Quebec bearing the LP's legal name; utility and internet-service bills; payroll and employee records; the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (NEQ) registration certificate; and any applicable provincial transport or freight-forwarding licence supporting the ISIC 5229 scope.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital contribution sourced from a corporate partner active in cryptocurrency, gambling, or other high-risk sectors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements and audited financial statements of the contributing partner; a written legal opinion confirming the absence of prohibited sources of funds; a full transaction-history reconciliation; flow-of-funds charts demonstrating the original economic origin of the contribution; and executed undertakings to maintain ongoing compliance with the PCMLTFA and Quebec AML directives.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusually large or unexplained pre-revenue deposits deposited before the first commercial charter contract is executed
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized partners' resolutions documenting the capital call and the escrow-purpose designation; the executed escrow agreement and term sheet; a capitalization table; the LP's audited or reviewed financial statements; and a forward 12-month treasury projection validated by the LP's external accountant and tax advisor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route the capital contribution as a SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer from the contributing partner's remitting bank to the LP's Canadian bank account. In the remittance information field, identify the payment as 'Capital contribution to limited partnership interest in CA_LP' and, where the sending or receiving bank requires a regulatory purpose code, assign the direct-investment / equity-participation classification consistent with that bank's International Transactions Reporting System (ITRS) reporting parameters. For CAD-denominated receipts, the domestic leg settles with finality through Lynx, Canada's real-time gross settlement system; USD and EUR receipts are cleared through Fedwire/CHIPS or TARGET2 respectively via the receiving Canadian bank's correspondent network. Pre-funding verification requirements: the LP must hold an active Quebec enterprise registration (NEQ); the partnership agreement and certificate of LP registration must be current; the bank mandate with authorized signatories must be executed; and source-of-funds documentation for the contribution must be pre-positioned with the bank's financial-crimes unit. The receiving bank will credit the Capital Escrow Account until the capital call subscription documentation, partnership register, and supporting KYC deliverables are fully validated.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail: SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for cross-border disbursements to aircraft operators, handling agents, fuel suppliers, airports, and navigation service providers; for high-value foreign-currency flows requiring cover payments, SWIFT MT202COV is used through the correspondent bank. CAD-denominated domestic disbursements clear via the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) for batch EFT or via Lynx RTGS where same-day finality is required. For trade-based settlements, commercial letters of credit are issued under UCP 600 using SWIFT MT700/MT707 in favor of charter operators and major fuel suppliers, or the LP may receive LC-backed payments from freight principals through a confirming Canadian bank. USD-denominated outbound payments may clear through Fedwire or CHIPS via the bank's US correspondent. FX execution should be consolidated through a single prime Canadian banking relationship to centralize counterparty risk and reduce spreads. The treasury architecture must strictly separate the capital/escrow stream from the operational disbursement stream to protect capital-account integrity and support the LP's audited financial record.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD foreign-exchange forward contracts executed with a licensed Canadian Schedule I bank or authorized FX dealer
FX swaps hedging staggered settlement dates between spot and forward legs
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for matched funding of USD-denominated aircraft charter liabilities
Over-the-counter vanilla currency options, including CAD/USD and CAD/EUR options, purchased from a domestic authorized bank
FX basis swaps used to hedge the CAD/USD funding spread
Deliverable CAD/EUR forward contracts for European charter counterparty settlement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual declaration (déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (RLRQ, c. P-44.1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before June 15 of each year for enterprises registered as of the preceding December 31; newly registered partnerships file the first annual declaration no later than June 15 of the year following registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty: CAD 500 to CAD 5,000 for a partnership; the Registrar may issue a notice of default and, after consecutive missed annual declarations, strike the limited partnership from the register or publish a proposal for dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return and T5013 slips (allocation of partnership income and loss to partners)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the partnership's fiscal period end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, no later than May 31 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file penalty: CAD 100 per day, maximum CAD 2,500; failure to issue T5013 slips attracts CAD 100 per slip with a minimum CAD 100; CRA may also reassess the partnership's income on a reasonable basis.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec partnership allocation report and required RL-series tax slips to registered partners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the partnership's fiscal period end; for a calendar-year partnership, no later than May 31 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted Quebec slips may result in penalties from CAD 25 to CAD 500 per slip depending on recurrence; Revenu Québec may reassess partners' Quebec-source income without the required documentation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A private Quebec limited partnership has no compulsory annual audit under the Civil Code of Quebec or the Quebec Limited Partnership Act. An independent audit becomes mandatory if the partnership is a reporting issuer, if the partnership agreement or financial covenant requires audited statements, or if the Canadian Transportation Agency or another aviation licensing authority imposes an audited financial statement as a condition of the air cargo charter broker operating certificate.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements may be prepared under IFRS or Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE); for income tax purposes, allocations are computed under Part 1 of the Income Tax Act (Canada) and Title IV of the Taxation Act (Quebec).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual declaration to the Quebec Enterprise Registrar must be checked for factual accuracy and must confirm the current general and limited partners, their registered addresses, and partnership interests. Any transfer of a partnership interest must be filed as a modification with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec within 15 days of the transfer; the annual declaration is not a substitute for that updating declaration. There is no separate annual UBO acknowledgment for a private limited partnership in Quebec.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (limited partners holding partnership interests)
Minute Book containing partnership resolutions and consents

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 to USD 650 per year (typical Quebec registered office or registered agent annual service fee)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 to USD 14,000 per year (typical independent audit fee for a small-to-mid-size air cargo charter partnership)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined federal-provincial general corporate headline rate (federal Part I 15% + Quebec general corporate rate 11.5%). The Quebec Limited Partnership (CA_LP) is fiscally transparent; no entity-level income tax is imposed on the LP itself, and each partner is taxable on the allocated share of partnership income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to this ISIC 5229 air-cargo charter brokerage LP. Effective reliefs: (i) federal small business deduction reducing the federal rate to 9% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income of a Canadian-controlled private corporation partner; (ii) Quebec SME deduction reducing the Quebec rate to 3.2% on the first CAD 500,000; (iii) federal SR&ED refundable investment tax credits up to 35% and Quebec refundable R&D tax credits up to 30% for qualifying air-logistics software/telemetry; (iv) GST/HST zero-rating for international air freight transportation services under Part VII of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act, with corresponding QST zero-rating; (v) availability of capital cost allowance and equipment-leasing deductions for aircraft charter assets held inside the LP.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 – Partnership Information Return (Canada Revenue Agency); mandatory CRA NETFILE electronic filing for partnerships with gross revenue above thresholds; includes T5013 Summary, Schedules and partner slips (T5013 Statement of Partnership Income).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due no later than 5 months after the last day of the partnership's fiscal period (e.g., December 31 fiscal period end -> May 31 of the following calendar year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business income of the partnership from air-cargo charter brokerage, freight forwarding commissions and ancillary logistics fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only income attributable to the Canadian partnership business; exclude income of non-resident partners earned outside Canada if not connected with the Canadian permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductible expenses including crew/travel, lease of aircraft capacity, communication, professional fees, and capital cost allowance claimed by the partnership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-arm’s-length management fees paid to a non-resident parent must be supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation; otherwise the deduction is denied and reportable on Form T106.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income (loss) of the partnership before allocation to partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The allocated net business income of a non-resident partner remains taxable in Canada under Part I of the Income Tax Act if it is income from a business carried on in Canada through the partnership.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital gains (losses) realized by the partnership during the fiscal period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disposition of taxable Canadian property by a partnership is reportable; a non-resident partner may be subject to Part I tax on the allocable capital gain and may claim treaty relief only with a valid Tax Residency Certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner identification block listing each partner's name, residence address, country of residence, and percentage interest in income and loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory identification of every non-resident partner; attach a certificate of residence or treaty form where reduced withholding or Part I exemption is claimed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of CAD 25 per day for each day the T5013 is outstanding, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500 under subsection 162(7) of the Income Tax Act; additional CAD 25 per day penalty for each missing or late T5013 partner slip; where the partnership has an assessable tax remittance obligation, a neglect/omission penalty of 5% of the unremitted amount plus 1% per month up to 12 months may also apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CO-17 – Déclaration de revenus d'une société de personnes (Declaration of a Partnership) filed with Revenu Québec; accompanied by Relevé 15 (RL-15) information slips issued to each partner for Quebec purposes.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due no later than 6 months after the end of the partnership's fiscal period (e.g., December 31 fiscal period end -> June 30 of the following calendar year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenus bruts d'entreprise (gross business revenue) from Quebec-source air cargo brokerage, charter arranging and forwarding commissions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only revenue attributable to activities carried on through a Quebec permanent establishment as determined under the Quebec Taxation Act and applicable DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dépenses admissibles (allowable expenses) claimed against business revenue, including charter purchase costs, insurance, professional fees, and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to a non-resident affiliate must satisfy Quebec's transfer pricing provision and be documented in the partnership's records; otherwise deductions are refused and penalties apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Bénéfice net ou perte nette de la société de personnes (net income or loss of the partnership).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner's allocable loss is generally available only to the extent the partner is taxable in Quebec; losses cannot be allocated to non-resident partners in a manner that creates a Quebec tax refund absent Quebec-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Part du revenu attribuée à chaque associé (share of income allocated to each partner); attach the statutory list of partners and their allocations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List the non-resident partner's Quebec allocation separately; a non-resident partner receiving the allocation must file a Quebec income tax return (TP-1-V or corporate TP-600 as applicable) and may claim treaty relief only with valid Quebec/P federal filings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of CAD 25 per day up to CAD 2,500 under the Quebec Taxation Act; late or missing RL-15 slips attract CAD 25 per day per slip up to CAD 2,500; interest at the Quebec prescribed rate accrues on unpaid balances; a wilful omission exposes the general partner to additional civil penalties and criminal prosecution under Quebec tax law.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 – Corporation Income Tax Return (Canada Revenue Agency) filed by any corporate partner or corporate general partner of the LP; filed via CRA NETFILE; federal Part I tax computation on Schedule 1.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due no later than 6 months after the end of the corporation's taxation year (e.g., December 31 corporate year-end -> June 30 of the following calendar year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income of the corporate partner before taxes, including the allocable share of the LP's T5013 partnership income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporate partner includes only Canadian-source business income allocable through the LP; foreign-source allocation is tracked separately and excluded where no Canadian nexus exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after applying non-capital loss carryovers, capital loss offsets, and treaty adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the 20-year non-capital loss carryforward and 3-year carryback; a non-resident corporate partner must compute taxable income earned in Canada in accordance with Part I and confirm treaty protection does not exceed the relief available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal Part I tax calculated at 15% on taxable income (general corporate rate), reduced by applicable deductions and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation must attach a Tax Residency Certificate to claim treaty-reduced rates on Canadian-source dividends or royalties; no treaty rate reduction is available absent the certificate and completed NR301 procedures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total federal taxes payable and instalment balance due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Instalments are required from non-resident corporate partners earning business income through a Canadian partnership; failure to remit attracts subsection 227(8) penalties and director liability under subsection 227.1.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital cost allowance computation for corporate assets held directly; partnership CCA is claimed inside the T5013, not in Schedule 8.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Avoid double claiming partnership CCA; the corporate partner claims only its own depreciable property. Non-resident partners may not allocate CCA in excess of their contributed capital unless the partnership agreement expressly provides otherwise.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under subsection 162(1): 5% of the balance due plus 1% per full month of delinquency up to 12 months; a repeated default adds 10%; gross negligence penalty under subsection 163(2) is 50% of the understated tax; criminal prosecution under section 238 may result in fines up to CAD 25,000 and imprisonment for directors who fail to file.
